long_biography.plain_text:
Environmental design became a defining feature of the communities Federico “Friedel” Stubbe developed in Puerto Rico. Growing up in Cidra, he learned from his father to build with the landscape, then trained as a civil engineer at Georgia Tech. His early subdivision work developed into the Sabanera communities; at Dorado Beach, the business combined homes with a restored resort and shared amenities.

Stubbe also helped establish TASIS Dorado, an English-language school conceived as part of the community's wider development. He has served the Puerto Rico homebuilders' association and advised civic redevelopment initiatives. The company's next generation, including his son Federico Jr. and daughter Ceciliana, now directs a broader portfolio, while Stubbe remains chairman and a strategic adviser.

A San Juan yacht-club tournament magazine explicitly calls Friedel Stubbe the owner of Prisa and Carolina's husband; Georgia Tech identifies Friedel's wife Carolina and son Federico, while the company roster separates Chairman Friedel from CEO Federico Jr. Thus the selected person is the father; vessel facts do not enter biography or wealth classification.

Neither his exact share percentage nor all current personal holdings are disclosed. The son, not Friedel, is current CEO and is credited by the industry association with leading post-2008 diversification; the father is described as a strategic adviser.

Positive founder history supports broad Self-made, but the father's influence on Friedel's building philosophy is not evidence of a transferred core enterprise. Searches for Forbes, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok and a personal website found no collision-safe personal profile; a LinkedIn result for Federico Stubbe Jr. is excluded. The PRISA domain is proposed solely as a company website.

Generic Property developer would overlap the same economic dimension; hotel and resort operations, casino and education tags would overstate or blur the father's own wealth-producing role.
